greeting: Is name_len bounded before any name byte is read?
Is every write to out bounded by capacity, and can the size arithmetic wrap?
Do all failure paths leave out[0] NUL when capacity > 0 and *written 0?
greeting_text: Does UTF-8 validation reject invalid lead bytes, truncated, bad-continuation, overlong, surrogate and above-U+10FFFF sequences while staying within length?
Does the printable check reject C0 controls, DEL and C1 controls, and does invalid UTF-8 win over a control?
greeting_main: Does greeting_main bound the argument scan, handle a NULL name and report usage, status and write errors?

findings.property: out-of-bounds read of name when name_len exceeds the readable name buffer (for example SIZE_MAX)
findings.severity: high if real: read past a borrowed caller buffer
findings.rationale: Illustrative example entry for the hello-world example, not a record of a real external review. A caller can pass a name_len larger than the readable name bytes; the UTF-8 scan would then read past the buffer. Each review unit names a source file, src/<unit>.c, and its locations are line numbers in that file. source_identity is the sha256 of json.dumps({path: sha256}, sort_keys=True) over the example files under src/, include/, tests/project/, fuzz/project/, specs/project/ and review/ (paths relative to examples/hello-world, review/ledger.json excluded).
findings.reproducer: tests/project/test_greeting.c: expect(max, SIZE_MAX, 128U, GREETING_NAME_TOO_LONG, "") and expect(max, GREETING_NAME_MAX + 1U, ...)

history.reason: Not a defect: validate() rejects name_len > GREETING_NAME_MAX at src/greeting.c:23 before greeting_check_text() reads any byte; the SIZE_MAX and 65-byte boundary tests cover it and the fuzz target checks it for every input length.
